images.title: Ten sevenths of chocolate
images.purpose: Show that 4 sevenths and 6 sevenths make 10 sevenths, which fill one whole bar with 3 sevenths over.
images.composition: Two chocolate bars stacked with wide space between them, left edges aligned, and one sum line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top: one flat chocolate bar of 7 equal blocks in a row; blocks 1 to 4 filled teal #0072B2, blocks 5 to 7 filled amber #E69F00, so the bar is full. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 outline around the whole top bar. Below: one bar of exactly the same size, left edges aligned, of 7 equal blocks; blocks 1 to 3 filled amber, blocks 4 to 7 plain. Centred below: one sum line. Exactly 2 bars, 14 blocks, 4 teal, 6 amber, 4 plain.

images.takeaway: Seven sevenths make one whole, so 10 sevenths is 1 and 3 sevenths.
images.description: Two same-size chocolate bars of 7 equal blocks: 4 teal and 3 amber blocks fill the first bar, and 3 more amber blocks sit in the second, so 4/7 + 6/7 = 10/7 = 1 3/7.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the full bar and say 7 sevenths make 1, then count the blocks left over.

image_decisions.why: A full bar plus 3 blocks shows a sum above one whole far better than words.
